posts.name: Person
posts.cooked:
The grep -E "ERROR|WARNING" server.log will return all the lines containing ERROR or WARNING. Then wc -w will count all the words in the matched lines, including words that are not ERROR or WARNING. Hence, option 4 is incorrect.

Since it is a log file, there cannot be an instance of ERROR and WARNING occurring together or more than once in a line. In my opinion, wc -l should work.

posts.name: Person
posts.cooked:
Jatin-Gera:

we want count of words not line

We do not want count of words, we want the count of occurences of ERROR and WARNING.

Please read this section of my earlier reply properly.

23f1000917:

Since it is a log file, there cannot be an instance of ERROR and WARNING occurring together or more than once in a line. In my opinion, wc -l should work.

I will explain it to you with the help of an example.

This is what a log file usually looks like :

2025-10-26 10:14:23,541 [INFO] Starting application...
2025-10-26 10:14:23,602 [DEBUG] Loading configuration from /etc/app/config.yaml
2025-10-26 10:14:23,708 [INFO] Database connection established
2025-10-26 10:14:25,012 [WARNING] Disk space running low (15% remaining)
2025-10-26 10:14:26,487 [ERROR] Failed to save user data: Connection timeout
2025-10-26 10:14:26,490 [DEBUG] Retrying database operation (attempt 2/3)
2025-10-26 10:14:27,021 [INFO] User 'admin' logged in
2025-10-26 10:14:30,004 [CRITICAL] Application crashed: OutOfMemoryError
2025-10-26 10:14:30,010 [INFO] Shutting down application...

The grep -E "ERROR|WARNING" server.log will output the lines :

2025-10-26 10:14:25,012 [WARNING] Disk space running low (15% remaining)
2025-10-26 10:14:26,487 [ERROR] Failed to save user data: Connection timeout

Each line will have ERROR or WARNING only once. Hence, counting the lines will be the same as counting the occurrences. Here, using -l will return the correct answer, which is 2.

wc -w is incorrect because it will count every single word in the line.

If you want to use wc -w, you must use the -o option in the grep command.
If you use -o, the output will look like the following :

WARNING
ERROR

Now, wc -w will give the correct answer, which is 2.

@sayan Please correct me if anything I said is incorrect, thank you.

posts.name: Sayan Ghosh
posts.cooked:
Yes, this is correct.

-w will count all words in the matched lines, which is not what we want.

  1. If you assume each line will have only one log-type, then wc -l counts number of lines that match which is your solution.
  2. If you expect a line can have multiple matches, then you have to do grep -o | wc -l to count the number of matches, not the number of words in lines that match, as -o will print ONLY matches, and on separate lines, then wc -l will print the number of lines generated by grep.
